mutants.why: gf128MulAlpha is XTS multiply-by-alpha (GF(2^128) left-shift-by-1); shifting by 2 yields the wrong per-block tweak for block 1 onward. apfsCrypto_matchesPublishedVectors (verifyApfsCryptoXtsVectors) pins IEEE-1619 Vector 1: QCOMPARE(vec1.toHex(), "917cf6...922e") -- the second 16-byte block (which uses the multiplied tweak) no longer matches.

mutants.find: const QByteArray r = xtsTransformUnit(key1, key2, firstDataUnit + u, unitData, encrypt);
mutants.replace: const QByteArray r = xtsTransformUnit(key1, key2, firstDataUnit, unitData, encrypt);
mutants.why: each XTS data unit must use tweak base firstDataUnit + u; dropping +u makes every unit share unit 0's tweak, so identical plaintext units encrypt identically. verifyApfsCryptoXtsVectors asserts QVERIFY(ctx2.left(512) != ctx2.mid(512)) on twoUnits=ptx+ptx -- the two halves would now be equal.

an APFS block maps to blockAddr*kApfsCryptoUnitsPerBlock (8) 512-byte crypto units; dropping the *8 makes xtsDecryptBlock use a different tweak base than xtsEncryptBlock, breaking the inverse. verifyApfsCryptoXtsVectors asserts QCOMPARE(xtsDecryptBlock(vek, 198, encBlock), block) where encBlock came from xtsEncryptBlock(vek, 198, block).

RFC 3394 unwrap must run exactly 6 outer rounds (j=5..0) to invert the 6-round wrap; running 5 leaves the integrity register A != 0xA6, so aesKeyUnwrap returns nullopt. verifyApfsCryptoHashHmacKeywrapVectors asserts QVERIFY(unwrapped.has_value()) and QCOMPARE(*unwrapped, key) on the RFC 3394 4.6 vector; also kills apfsKeybag_reproducesHarvestedFileVaultBlobs' QVERIFY(kek.has_value()).

the RFC 3394 integrity check must reject when the recovered A block is not all-0xA6 (fail closed on a wrong key); inverting the guard returns nullopt on a CORRECT unwrap and a garbage key on a wrong one -- a fail-open. verifyApfsCryptoHashHmacKeywrapVectors asserts QVERIFY(unwrapped.has_value()) on the correct-key vector, which now fails.

a keybag block is valid if its magic is EITHER keybag type; the && guard rejects only blocks that are neither, while || rejects every block (magic can equal at most one type), so parseKeybagBlock always returns empty. apfsKeybag_reproducesHarvestedFileVaultBlobs (verifyApfsKeybagBlockTopology) asserts QCOMPARE(parsed.size(), 2) on the built container keybag.

the inner keyblob is the DER [0xA3] context field; matching 0xA2 instead never captures it, so keyblob stays empty, wrappedKey is never assigned, and parseKeyBlob returns false (wrappedKey.size() != 40). apfsKeybag_reproducesHarvestedFileVaultBlobs asserts QVERIFY(parseKeyBlob(parsed.at(1).keydata, &vp)) and QCOMPARE(vp.wrappedKey, wrappedVek).

the guard must reject entries whose packed size EXCEEDS the block (else the entry writes overflow it); inverting to < both rejects a well-formed sub-block and accepts an oversized one. apfsKeybag_failsClosedOnMalformedEntry asserts QVERIFY(!buildKeybagBlock(good-entry...).isEmpty()) (now empty) and QVERIFY(buildKeybagBlock(8192-byte keydata...).isEmpty()) (now non-empty).

0x87 is the IEEE Std 1619-2007 GF(2^128) reduction polynomial, XORed into the next XTS tweak only when an alpha-multiply carries out of byte 15. apfsCrypto_xtsGf128ReductionConstantIsExercised drives xtsEncrypt over a 512-byte data unit (32 blocks / 31 alpha-multiplies) whose tweak sequence carries, then QCOMPAREs the ciphertext against an INDEPENDENT reference computed from the FIPS-197-pinned aesEcbEncryptBlock primitive and the literal correct constant 0x87 (the reference is validated against published IEEE-1619 Vector 1). The test asserts a carry is actually consumed (usedReduction) and that ref(0x87) != ref(0x86), so the 0x86 mutant diverges at the first carrying block and the exact-bytes QCOMPARE(cipher, ref87) turns red. Not a symmetric round trip -- the expected bytes come from a reference built with the correct constant, independent of the source's gf128MulAlpha reduction.
